selections.comment: LATIN FIVE has been running well on the all-weather in recent starts, but Paul Midgley's charge has been more effective on turf previously. The eight-year-old had a mixed campaign last season but he's undeniably well handicapped now and if continuing his recent level of form, it would come as no surprise were he to come out on top. Jamie's Choice finished second off this mark at Redcar when last seen in September and is respected, along with Golden Prosperity.

selections.comment: This looks competitive and only a tentative vote can go to UNTIL DAWN, who has shown clear progress since being switched to handicaps. Alan Brown's filly hit the woodwork when in search of her hat-trick at Southwell three weeks ago, but a switch to turf could prompt further improvement and a low draw is favourable too. Natsumi recorded a narrow success at Lingfield last time out and is an obvious danger. Market support for Solar Biricz should be noted.

Flying Scotsman has been running with credit at Newcastle recently so must enter calculations, along with Arctic Fox, who drops in class.

selections.comment: Having weakened inside the final furlong to finish seventh over 1m2f at Beverley in August last year, Stay In The Game warrants consideration reverting to novice company and dropping in trip. However, preference is for three-year-old TAWASOL. The Havana Grey colt arrives on the back of a close-up second at Wolverhampton and he ticks the most boxes. Monsieur Fudge is also noted sporting first-time blinkers.

selections.comment: The combination of a 182-day break and return to 7f proved just the tonic recent Musselburgh winner DOOMSDAY. The six-year-old's 5lb penalty is effectively negated by Tom Kiely-Marshall's 5lb claim in the plate and a quick double could be on the cards. Coconut Bay finished only a neck behind the selection and, racing off an unchanged mark, she is feared most. Market support for either Beltane or Darbucks would be interesting.

selections.comment: It could pay to focus on those who have a recent run under their belt, namely LUCIUS AURELIUS and Kisskodi. The latter only found one too good when a well-backed favourite on his seasonal/handicap debut at Newcastle and should go well again, but Kevin Ryan's charge shades the verdict coming out of stall one. The rail draw should suit this frontrunner, who arguably produced his best effort to date when returning at Southwell. Go On Rosie may fare best of the rest.

selections.comment: Past C&D winner ACT OF VIOLENCE edges the vote in what looks a fiercely competitive finale. He finished last season with two solid efforts in 0-80 company, appears best on this forecast quick ground and is the choice of stable jockey David Allan. Tim Easterby's other runner Mister Sox likes it here, recording both career victories at this venue, and he shouldn't be underestimated, while Daytona Lady is a capable type.

selections.comment: Paroda Diva is the only one with racecourse experience and will have benefitted for last week's introduction at Bath. However, she looks worth taking on and VIAMARIE makes plenty of appeal. A half-sister to the smart sprinter First Folio, she represents George Boughey's in-form yard and could prove good enough at the first time of asking. Very Mindful is another debutant to keep an eye on for the future.

selections.comment: A competitive affair with no less than six winners on show. Life Is Beautiful left a good impression when scoring over course and distance in November, while Bijoux made a winning debut last month when successful at Southwell. Badiyah is a newcomer to note.

selections.comment: COSMIC YEAR is prominent in the betting market for next month's 2000 Guineas at Newmarket and is difficult to oppose on his reappearance. The son of Kingman trounced his rivals over 7f at Sandown in September and this should set him up nicely for a tilt at the big one. Honved failed to confirm the promise of his debut second at Wolverhampton when disappointing at Doncaster, so newcomers National Park and Hit Squad could prove bigger threats.

selections.comment: The winner of two of his last three starts over 7f at Southwell, GRAND KARAT has flourished since being gelded and appeals strongly returning from a break off a potentially workable rating. The versatile son of Gleneagles was a close second on his only previous attempt over C&D and could go one better if he copes with stepping up in class. United Approach has won fresh from an absence in the past and is feared most on that basis, while Yorkshire and Blue Prince are others who could have a big say.

selections.comment: Papabella made good strides on turf last season and resumes off a workable mark. However, there is a slight query about her record when fresh and others could take advantage of any rustiness, with the low-mileage RIFT VALLEY suggested as the first one to consider. The James Fanshawe-trained filly was a respectable fourth, despite the jockey dropping the reins, in a Newcastle maiden last month and could be a different proposition debuting in a handicap with her match-fitness topped up. Four Adaay and Kensington Agent are other solid contenders.

selections.comment: RUMBA BAY continued her progression when landing the spoils at Wolverhampton last month. Having previously won at Chelmsford, reverting to Polytrack holds no fear for David Evans' filly and a third career victory could be on the cards. The biggest threat may emerge from Off The Bench, who offered plenty of promise on his third-placed stable bow at the Essex track 13 days ago. Take The Boat is also noted on her return to 7f.

selections.comment: Captain Brett has posted two creditable efforts in defeat since entering handicap company over C&D in February and he is one of the likelier winners. However, David Simcock's gelding could prove vulnerable to an improver and preference is for the unexposed JUSTENZIA. An opening mark of 63 looks workable for the daughter of Ghaiyyath and she is likely to relish tonight's step up in trip. Staffordshire could also have a say if settling better.

selections.comment: James Tate has been amongst the winners of late and he appears to have found a great opening for STORM FREE, who has earned a rating of 83. If improving from two to three years, he will likely get the better of Dan Tucker. Jedd O'Keeffe's charge is rated 4lb below the selection and has had one more run, but a gelding operation since finishing second at Redcar in October could potentially unlock another gear. Sharp Call is also noted.

selections.comment: Cameron Highlander made a pleasing debut when third over 1m at Newcastle last month and he looks best of the experienced runners, but at least one or two of the newcomers might prove to be better than him. The one who makes most appeal is Harry Eustace's SEA OF KINGS, who cost 250,000 euros as a foal and is certainly bred to have plenty of ability being a full-brother to dual Group 1 winner Sea Of Class. Munsif must enter calculations representing Roger Varian, while Belaya River is also of interest.

Zarathos shaped with promise when third at Southwell in February and is unlikely to be far away, along with the consistent Antiquity.

The gelded son of Awtaad should come forward from a recent spin at Saint Cloud and is taken to repel the challenge of Real Dream. Align The Stars has some strong handicap form in the book and is no back number.

selections.comment: GENTLE WARRIOR impressed when winning by nine and a half lengths over C&D when last seen and could have plenty more to offer now he has proven himself capable over this distance. The handicapper dished out a 9lb hike for that but he's still lightly raced and might be able to kick on. War Hawk is feared most, turned out under a penalty after last week's Lingfield triumph. Handicap debutants Anglophile, Epimeteo and Sourdough also command respect.

selections.comment: DINO MAGIC was beaten less than a length by a much higher rated rival in a match at Exeter last month. Paul Nicholls' inmate looks potentially well treated on his handicap debut if that form is taken literally, and this extra distance should also suit. Myfanwy's Magic will appreciate the return to today's longer trip based on his second at Ludlow back in November, while Basman Palace got his act together when scoring at Wincanton and remains on an attractive mark.

selections.comment: Rascallion made a winning stable debut for Henrietta Knight when successful in maiden company at Wincanton. He will likely have a say in proceedings once again, despite carrying a penalty, but is conceding plenty of weight to the four-year-old NARDARAN. The latter made a promising debut over timber at Kempton before struggling in the Listed Scottish Triumph Hurdle and he gets another chance at this more suitable level. Vaguely Royal is preferred of the remainder.

selections.comment: Dirty Den finished just in front of PHOENIX RISEN (third) when runner-up here last month, but his jumping fell apart at Hereford last time, and Jeremy Scott's charge is fancied to turn the tables. The latter is only 2lb higher than when landing a tougher contest at Wincanton at the end of last year and another bold bid is anticipated. Taritino has been in the mix here of late and could land a blow.

However, Michael Hawker's gelding is 2lb out of the handicap and it could be worth taking a punt on SAINT BIBIANA. The eight-year-old should have learned plenty from her third-placed chase bow at Southwell last month and she looks more than capable of scoring in this discipline. Another Day Out makes more appeal than Anytrixwilldo.

selections.comment: TINY TETLEY arrives on the back of a career-best victory at Exeter and another small-field affair looks an ideal opportunity for him to dominate once more. The seven-year-old is effectively racing off a 1lb lower mark if taking Callum Pritchard's 5lb claim into account and another bold bid is forecast. The biggest threat could emerge from Florencethemachine, who may enjoy reverting to timber, ahead of the downgraded Hardy Du Seuil.

selections.comment: Despite some less than fluent jumping, BUMPY EVANS completed a double over an extended 2m3f at Ffos Las three days ago with something in hand. The dual 3m point-to-point winner looks a likely improver up in trip and a 7lb penalty may not be enough to prevent a hat-trick. Unspeakable is entitled to build on his fourth-placed reappearance at Chepstow last month and the seven-year-old may serve the most resistance to the selection, ahead of C&D winner School For Scandal.

selections.comment: BIG BOY BARNEY offered plenty of encouragement on his fourth-placed Rules debut at Warwick last month. The winner subsequently finished a cracking second in a Grade 2 at the Aintree Festival and Fergal O'Brien's charge is unlikely to bump into anything of that calibre here. Calvino was too bad to be true when well beaten in sixth at Chepstow 20 days ago, but a reproduction of his debut fourth at Ascot would see him in the mix. Daring To Dream is the pick of the remainder.
